description: 4 tactical challenges for Black in the Englund Gambit (1.d4 e5), the cheeky countergambit. Punish White's pawn grab with Qe7 tricks, Nxe5 regains, and rapid development after 3...Qe7.

drills.briefExplanation: Nxe5 regains the pawn with tempo. After Bf4, Ng6 attacks the bishop, and d6 solidifies the center.
drills.description: Regain the gambit pawn with Nxe5. After White develops the bishop, kick it with Ng6 gaining tempo, then solidify with d6.
drills.explanation: Nxe5 is the point of the Englund Gambit — Black sacrifices a pawn on move 1 to regain it on move 4 with a tempo. The knight on e5 is perfectly centralized: it attacks c4 and d3, supports ...d5, and cannot easily be kicked out. White develops with Bf4, attacking the knight, but Black simply plays Ng6!, gaining a tempo by attacking the bishop. The knight on g6 is well-placed: it eyes f4 and h4, supports ...e5, and prepares ...Bg7. White retreats Bg3, and Black plays d6, solidifying the center. Black has regained the pawn, developed two pieces, and White has nothing to show for the opening. The Englund's opening trap has worked perfectly — Black is already slightly better.
drills.name: Regaining the Pawn

drills.briefExplanation: Qb4+ exploits White's slow development. After Bd2 blocks, Qxb2 wins a pawn with tempo.
drills.description: Punish White's bishop development with the Qb4+ check. After White blocks, snatch the b2 pawn and retreat the queen to safety.
drills.explanation: Qb4+ is the Englund's signature trick — Black exploits White's undeveloped queenside with a devastating check. The queen on b4 attacks the b2 pawn and creates multiple threats. White's only sensible block is Bd2, interposing the bishop, but Black simply plays Qxb2!, winning a clean pawn. The b2 pawn falls because White's queenside is completely undeveloped — the knight is still on b1 and the rook on a1 is undefended. White develops with Nc3, attacking the queen, but Black retreats Qb6, keeping the extra pawn. Black is up a pawn with a solid position. This Qb4+ idea is why White must be careful in the Englund — one slow move and the b2 pawn drops.
drills.name: Queen Check Wins a Pawn

drills.briefExplanation: Qb4+ punishes the greedy e4 push. After Bd2, Qxb2 wins a pawn and Qxa2 grabs a second.
drills.description: After White pushes e4 to hold the pawn, strike with Qb4+. White blocks with Bd2, but Black wins the b2 pawn and retreats to safety.
drills.explanation: Qb4+ is even stronger after White's greedy 4.e4 — White tried to hold the extra pawn with a pawn push, but this weakens the queenside further. The queen check on b4 is devastating: White must block with Bd2. Black plays Qxb2!, winning the b-pawn because White's queenside is completely undeveloped. White develops with Nc3, attacking the queen, but Black retreats Qb6, keeping the extra pawn and eyeing b2. Black is up a pawn with a solid position. The e4 push was a mistake — it didn't consolidate anything and just gave Black a target. This is the Englund's punishment for greed.
drills.name: Punishing the e4 Push

drills.briefExplanation: Nxe5 regains the pawn. After e4, Nf6 develops with tempo, and d5 strikes at White's center.
drills.description: Regain the pawn with Nxe5. After White pushes e4, develop the knight with tempo, then blast the center with d5.
drills.explanation: Nxe5 regains the gambit pawn, and after White pushes e4 to build a center, Black develops with Nf6, attacking the e4 pawn with tempo. The knight on f6 is perfectly placed: it pressures e4, prepares ...d5, and supports kingside castling. White defends with Bd3, but Black strikes with d5!, the thematic Englund counter. The d5 pawn break challenges White's center immediately — if White plays exd5, Black recaptures with the knight and has a beautiful centralized position. If White doesn't capture, Black will play dxe4 and White's center collapses. Black has full equality with active piece play, all from a 'dubious' gambit. The Englund's ...d5 break is the great equalizer.
drills.name: The d5 Counterstrike
